rules.name: Get-DomeniaMigrationPlan
rules.contract: Get-DomeniaMigrationPlan $Legacy $Current [-SupportedSchemaVersions @('11')] [-PreservedNames ...] [-Trigger Explicit|Startup]. $Legacy = {ConfigFiles; Domain (from the DN columns, read by the caller); Stores=[{Kind=Objets|Parc|Recherches|Secrets|Liens; Path; Rows; Links}]}. $Current = {ConfigFiles; Domain; Database={Name,SchemaVersion,DomeniaSchema,BaseDn} or $null; Tables (table -> row count); Links}. A store is imported only into an empty table, one source per table, first one found wins. Legacy domain is checked against the current domain. Trigger 'Startup' blocks. A refused plan turns every write into 'Reporter'. Returns Allowed, Blockers, Steps (Kind, Action, Planned, Source, Target, Reason, Key, Item), Trace (Ancien, Nouveau, Decision), Copy/Adopt/Import/Add/Keep/Skip/Refused/Rejected/DeferredCount, WriteCount, RequiresBackup, ModifiesLegacyDatabase, SourceKept. Caveat: links are deduplicated as most recent per computer.

rules.name: Get-DomeniaMigratedState
rules.contract: Get-DomeniaMigratedState $Current $Plan. Returns the projected {Domain, ConfigFiles, Database, Tables, Links} and touches nothing. A refused plan changes nothing. Copied names, imported row counts and added links are appended; nothing present before is removed.

rules.name: Test-DomeniaMigrationIdempotent
rules.contract: Test-DomeniaMigrationIdempotent $Legacy $Current [-Trigger]. Plans, projects the result, then plans again on it. Idempotent = (second WriteCount = 0) and no Copier onto an existing config and no new duplicate computer key and no lost link. Returns Idempotent, Applied, FirstWrites, SecondWrites, DuplicateLinks, OverwrittenConfig, LostLinks, First, Second, State. This is the dry-run proof shown before apply.

Purging sync_state deletes the base_dn that Get-DomeniaDatabasePath (Core:19909) uses to adopt the legacy database. The next session would then create Domains\<hash>\Domenia.db and the manual associations would become unreachable. The Index purge must reset the sync_state row, never delete it.

An incremental IndexBulk still pending in Persistence.Pending after an Index purge would rewrite highest_usn on an incomplete index. Refresh would then continue incrementally without noticing; the only safeguard today is a count of 0 (Core:14300).

Deleting any row of user_machine_links outside the queue breaks LocalStore's LinkHash baseline: later saves would be refused as conflicts (Storage.Worker:142-146). That is why the whole table, observed links included, stays out of the purge.
Inconsistent date formats: a link's When is local 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss' (Core:18499) while Presence uses UTC 'o'. Text comparison is unreliable; use julianday and keep NULL results.
Get-DomeniaPurgePlan's Keeps* flags are constants (Cache.Model:369). Step B already rejected a rule that returned constants, so only a behavioral test in the worker counts as proof.

Maps.decisionNeeded:
The product owner needs to decide five things:
(1) What a purge of a ticked category means:
- (a) clear the whole category (Observations, Snapshots, Index can be rebuilt), or
- (b) apply the bounds, in which case the numbers must be aligned. The rule says 90 d / 200000, 180 d / 5000, 730 d / 100000; the code applies 30 d, 5000 per scope, 20 queries per scope, 20000 history rows and 10000 runs.
(2) Which links count as manual associations: 'Manual' and 'Saisie manuelle' only, or also 'Import CSV'? A CSV can carry any text in its Source column.
(3) Whether the history of those associations is protected too. That covers user_machine_history rows, the D050 relations journal, the automatic 20000-row cap in LocalStore, and the orphan cleanup in Start-PruneOrphanLinks, which deletes manual links today.
(4) Whether the Logs category may delete the audit log Domenia.log, or only rotated files (.1, startup and login logs older than 60 days).
(5) Confirm that Receipts stays entirely non-purgeable in D029, including resolved ones, with no archiving despite the 512-receipt cap in ReceiptStore.

rules.name: Get-DomeniaPersistenceLabel
rules.contract: param([int]$Pending=0,[int]$Failed=0,[bool]$Suspended=$false) -> string. Priority: Suspended gives 'En memoire uniquement : enregistrement suspendu apres des echecs. Reprise dans Fiabilite.'; then Failed>0 gives 'En memoire : N enregistrement(s) en echec, nouvel essai prevu.'; then Pending>0 gives 'En memoire : N modification(s) a enregistrer.'; otherwise 'Enregistre.'. rules.contract: param([string]$StoredVersion,[string]$BaseVersion,[bool]$RowExists=$true) -> {Apply,Conflict,Reason}. A new row is applied; an unknown base version or a different stored version is a conflict and nothing is written over it. The worker cannot call module functions, so Storage.Worker.ps1:143-145 repeats the same check inline. Keep that inline check; no new call site.

rules.name: Get-DomeniaCacheReadPolicy
rules.contract: Takes [bool]HasSnapshot, IdentityMatches, FreshReadConfirmed, Offline, WriteUncertain. Returns CanView = CanCopy = HasSnapshot -and IdentityMatches; CanEdit = view -and Fresh -and -not Offline -and -not WriteUncertain; Historical = view -and -not Fresh; CanRetry = -not WriteUncertain -and -not Offline. Reason precedence: Aucune donnee > Identite non confirmee > Operation a verifier > Consultation historique hors ligne > relecture necessaire > Lecture AD confirmee. PS 5.1: [bool] parameters reject $null and strings, so cast every argument with [bool](...).

rules.name: Get-DomeniaCacheCatalogRows
rules.contract: Takes Entries {Scope, Source, Dc, Reader, Rows, ObservedUtc} and NowUtc. Returns one row per entry {Perimetre, Source, Controleur, Lecteur, Objets, Observe dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm or 'inconnu', Age 'N j|h|min', Usage 'Consultation historique. Aucune modification sans relecture AD.'}. Pure, no I/O.

rules.name: Get-DomeniaRecordFreshness
rules.contract: Reads Record.Times[Nature]. Returns {State Fresh|Stale|Unknown|Historical, ObservedUtc, LastAttemptUtc, Label}. Attributes is Fresh for 900 s or less (Get-DomeniaFreshnessPolicy :91). A cached render has ObservedUtc=$null, so State is Unknown. Use it as the FreshReadConfirmed source, which does not depend on SelectionLoad.

rules.name: Set-DomeniaObservationTime
rules.contract: Records LastAttemptUtc for one nature, and ObservedUtc only when Succeeded. Already called by Show-AdObjectResult (Core:21938).

rules.name: Get-DomeniaErrorDecision
rules.contract: Takes Structured (from Get-DomeniaStructuredError, Domenia-Guard.Model.ps1:2) and Text. Returns {Category, Retryable, Explanation, NextAction}. Category Network covers kind Unavailable, native 53/64/67/81/1722..., and HRESULT 0x800706BA/0x8007203A/0x80070035/0x80072EE7 (:112). Category Timeout covers native 1460/258/121 or timeout text. This is the only existing classifier that turns a worker failure into 'network lost'.

rules.name: Get-DomeniaDisabledHelp
rules.contract: Takes -Action and -Reason (ValidateSet includes Offline and Stale). Returns {ToolTip, HelpText, Route}. For Offline the text is 'Hors ligne : seules les donnees deja lues sont consultables.' with route TabGuard (:790). Use it for the tooltips of disabled write controls.

rules.name: Test-DomeniaProviderAdmission
rules.contract: Existing precedent (D018/D027): during a provider backoff only Background reads are refused; Explicit reads are still admitted. Relevant to the decision on the manual Retry button.

rules.name: Resolve-DomeniaDirectoryReachability (TO ADD, D030 section after line 389)

Maps.decisionNeeded:
The product owner has three decisions to make:
1. Manual 'Reessayer la lecture' while offline. Either keep it enabled, following the D018/D027 precedent where Test-DomeniaProviderAdmission still admits Explicit reads (CanRetry is then documented as automatic retry only), or disable it as the rule's CanRetry=$false says (asserted by Cache.Tests.ps1:134). Disabling it means the only way back online is another successful AD read.
2. Depth of consultation for a fiche that is cached or failed. Either it stays visible but greyed (host IsEnabled=$false: no tab switching, scrolling or copying), which is today's safe behavior, or it becomes navigable read-only, which requires listing every mutating control in the fiche, not only Get-WriteControlMap.
3. Whether the cache explorer (Get-DomeniaCacheCatalogRows) is required to close D030, and if so whether a memory-only source (IndexInfo plus the visit cache) is enough, or whether the SQLite history is needed (new pinned worker operation).

rules.name: Get-DomeniaStorageLayout
rules.contract:
Params:
- Mode: UserLocal, Portable or Compatible.
- InstallRoot: the parent of wad.
- UserLocalRoot: LocalApplicationData.
- Writable: an IDictionary keyed by category or by path; the most restrictive answer wins.
- PortableHasData, NetworkDrives.

Returns {Ready, Mode, ModeSource (Explicite or Deduit), DataRoot, Errors[], Notices[], Categories[]}. Each category has {Category, Label, Path, ReadAlsoFrom, Rights, WriteRequired, MustBeLocal, Writable ($null when not observed), State, Error, Fallback=''}. State is one of: Pret, Non localise, Distant refuse, Lecture seule attendue, Non verifie, Non inscriptible.

Category paths:
- Preference: DataRoot\Preferences, ReadAlsoFrom = DataRoot and InstallRoot\wad.
- Cache: DataRoot. That is InstallRoot\wad\data in Portable, UserLocalRoot\Domenia\Data otherwise.
- Receipt: always UserLocalRoot\Domenia\Receipts.

It never redirects. A missing root gives '' paths plus an error. Compatible mode is deduced only from PortableHasData, never from rights, and is announced in Notices. Ready is false while any WriteRequired category is not observed, so the caller must decide per category and not gate on Ready.

rules.name: Join-DomeniaReleasePath
rules.contract: Joins paths as text only, with no provider lookup. Returns '' when the root is empty. This is why a missing profile produces no invented path. Use it for any new path the rule exposes.

rules.name: Test-DomeniaReleaseMapKey
rules.contract: Key lookup that works on a hashtable, an ordered dictionary or a generic Dictionary[string,bool] (PS 5.1 explicit IDictionary.Contains). The layout reads Writable through it, so the caller can pass observed rights keyed by category or by full path.

rules.name: Get-DomeniaPreferenceMigrationPlan (proposed, to add after Domenia-Release.Model.ps1:1415)
rules.contract:
Pure. Inputs: the layout object and observed files [{Path, Exists, Bytes, IsReparse, ValidJson}]. Migrated names default to 'Domenia.settings.json', the only preference ever written.

Output: Steps [{Action, Source, Target, Reason}] plus Errors. Action is one of:
- Copier: source in DataRoot, target in the Preference Path, target absent, source valid JSON of at most 1 MiB and not a reparse point.
- Conserver: the target exists and is never overwritten.
- Ignorer: the source is under InstallRoot\wad (shipped, pinned payload), or is invalid, oversized or a reparse point.
- Refuser: Preference State is not Pret. The error names the Preference path and no other destination is proposed.

Rules: never Supprimer or Deplacer, since the sources are kept (the rule's own Rights text). No migration across modes. Running the plan again on the resulting state gives zero Copier steps.

rules.name: Get-DomeniaMigrationPlan / Test-DomeniaMigrationIdempotent (reference only, do not reuse)
rules.contract: ADCC to Domenia migration in the app folder. PreservedNames includes Domenia.theme.cfg and Domenia.ui-profile.cfg, and a Startup trigger is refused for data. It does not fit a DataDir root to DataDir\Preferences copy. Take only its idempotence check (a second plan writes nothing) and the 'existing file always wins' principle.
